label: input token x in the first three original positions
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter x during the original phase, almost entirely at positions t=0..2 (weak residual at t=3, nothing later, nothing at the delimiter or in the copy phase). About 27% of all x inputs activate it, and none of the other tokens do. Magnitude falls with position: x at t=0 gives the largest values (~1.0 of max, 42% of mass), t=1 is lower (~0.8, 37%), t=2 lower again (~0.45-0.7, 20%). An x that repeats an earlier x is strongly suppressed (e.g. x at t=1 right after x at t=0 is near 0). Activation does not depend on surrounding tokens or L, apart from the position effect.

issues: The explanation's claim that a repeated x is strongly suppressed (x at t=1 right after x at t=0 is near 0) is false. On the test split, (in_tok==x)&(t==1)&(orig(0)==x) has precision 1.0, so every such step fires. Dev misses show 'x x l w ...' with the second x at 0.62, while a fresh x at t=1 is about 0.77-0.86. More generally, x at t in {1,2} with an earlier x has test precision 1.0, recall 0.032 and mass recall 0.018. That is about 0.57x the average magnitude: reduced, not suppressed.

Everything else checks out. Activation is 100% in the original phase (1 copy-phase step out of 52.7k, 0 at the delimiter). Every active step has in_tok x. Mass shares by t are 0.424 / 0.369 / 0.200 / 0.008 for t=0/1/2/3, with nothing at t>=4.
The 2865 test misses are all weak x at t=3 (0.01-0.31). They hold only 0.8% of the mass, and adding t=3 drops precision to 0.80 (F1 0.887), so leaving t=3 out of the predicate is justified.
The 42 test false positives cluster on a few prefixes like '3 h x' and '3 o x' (x at t=2 after a leading 3). This is a tiny, specific pocket and is not worth encoding.
The predicate reproduces on test: precision 0.999, recall 0.946, F1 0.972, mass recall 0.992.
